rationale: The hypothesis posits a strict dichotomy: complete loss-of-function nullizygosity of PLAA produces an embryonic- or fetal-lethal phenotype characterized by multi-organ dysplasia on prenatal ultrasound, whereas hypomorphic variants permit fetal survival and cause an isolated postnatal neurodegenerative disorder. While literature confirms that hypomorphic alleles permit live birth followed by an infantile-lethal neurodegenerative/neurodevelopmental course with progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and seizures (Hall et al. 2017; Falik Zaccai et al. 2017), the claim regarding complete nullizygosity is conflicted. First, Plaa-null mice survive through gestation to perinatal lethality with central nervous system malformations (exencephaly/microcephaly) rather than non-viable early embryonic arrest or widespread multi-organ dysplasia (Falik Zaccai et al. 2017). Second, while fetal demise and prenatal ultrasound detection of biallelic PLAA variants have been reported in deceased fetuses (Huang et al. 2023), the phenotype remains primarily restricted to the central nervous system (neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies) rather than a generalized multi-organ dysplastic syndrome.

evidence.text: Seven patients from consanguineous kindreds presenting at 2-4 months of age with progressive microcephaly, spastic quadriparesis, and global developmental delay harbored a homozygous missense variant (p.Leu752Phe) in PLAA. Complete Plaa knockout mice survived gestation and exhibited perinatal lethality with microcephaly/exencephaly and reduced brain PGE2 levels.

evidence.text: Hypomorphic mutations in the ubiquitin adaptor protein PLAA in humans and mice result in an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome with progressive microcephaly and intractable seizures due to impaired endolysosomal trafficking of synaptic proteins.

source.title: PLAA mutations cause a lethal infantile epileptic encephalopathy by disrupting ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation of synaptic proteins
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: In both human and mouse, hypomorphic mutations in the ubiquitin adaptor protein PLAA cause an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome with seizures. Resulting from perturbed endolysosomal degradation, Plaa mutant neurons accumulate K63-polyubiquitylated proteins and synaptic membrane proteins

evidence.text: Retrospective whole-exome sequencing in deceased fetuses with ultrasound abnormalities identified compound heterozygous loss-of-function variants in PLAA associated with severe fetal neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies (NDMSBA).

conflicts: Plaa complete knockout mice exhibit late gestational/perinatal lethality with cranial/CNS defects (exencephaly/microcephaly) rather than early embryonic lethality or widespread extra-neural multi-organ dysplasia.

Biallelic human PLAA variants identified in deceased fetuses with ultrasound anomalies present with severe central nervous system anomalies (NDMSBA) rather than established multi-organ syndromic malformations.

Falik Zaccai et al. classify the postnatally viable homozygous L752F missense change as a 'loss-of-function' allele, challenging the sharp categorical boundary between missense hypomorphs and loss-of-function nullizygosity.

new_directions.question_text: Do human fetuses with complete biallelic PLAA null mutations (nonsense, frameshift, or canonical splice disruptions) exhibit structural anomalies outside the central nervous system on fetal autopsy and imaging?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether PLAA nullizygosity truly drives multi-organ dysplasia or exclusively causes lethal primary microcephaly and neural tube/brain closure defects will clarify if non-CNS findings are genuine features of the molecular pathology.

new_directions.question_text: What is the residual functional activity of the p.Leu752Phe variant compared to true nonsense null alleles in human cell models of ubiquitin-dependent endolysosomal sorting?
new_directions.rationale: Quantifying residual enzymatic or protein-interaction capacity will formally test if postnatal survival requires a threshold of PLAA activity.
